title: Erdős–Faudree conjecture on Hamiltonian subsets of regular Dirac graphs
statement: Let $G$ be an $(n+1)$-regular graph on $2n$ vertices. A subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ is called Hamiltonian when the induced subgraph $G[S]$ contains a Hamilton cycle. **Erdős–Faudree conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that $G$ has at least $c2^{2n}$ Hamiltonian subsets. The source presents this as a question of Erdős and Faudree; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
source_name: Wanting Sun, Shunan Wei and Donglei Yang, “Clique factors in random samplings of regular graphs”, arXiv:2512.20287 (2025).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2503.01826](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01826).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20287

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “This conjecture was resolved by Cuckler and Kahn . {We refer the reader to a survey of Sudakov where various measures of robustness and relevant results are collected.”
